entries.name: Armidale

facts.claim: Armidale is a small city of about 24,500 in the New England region, noted for colonial-era architecture, centres of education and culture, and nearby wilderness and gorge country; Wikivoyage calls it Australia's highest city by altitude.
It sits roughly halfway between Sydney and Brisbane at the junction of the New England Highway and Waterfall Way, and is home to the University of New England.
Its sights include NERAM, Saumarez Homestead and the Waterfall Way parks; the city is also the gateway to Oxley Wild Rivers and New England national parks.

entries.name: New England National Park

entries.name: Kwiambal National Park

facts.claim: Pronounced Kigh-am-bal: a secluded reserve past Inverell near the NSW-Queensland border, with swimming, scenic picnics, cheap accommodation, mountain biking, birdwatching and fishing; day trippers travel in from Ashford and Inverell.
The Severn and Macintyre rivers flow through the park and converge below Macintyre Falls; the park is studded with granite outcrops and also has Ashford Caves.
Macintyre Falls lookout is next to a well-equipped picnic area with swimming, hiking and fishing nearby; walks include Junction, Rock Pool and Slippery Rock tracks.

NPWS alerts (2026-10-18): Limestone Caves closed until further notice (since Sept 2020); Lavender Vale Homestead closed to bookings, Lavender Vale Cottage open. No park entry fee (not on the fee-collecting list).

entries.name: Warrabah National Park

facts.claim: Warrabah National Park, near Tamworth and Uralla, offers camping, bushwalking, fishing, swimming, canoeing and birdwatching beside the Namoi River; always open but may close for fire danger or flooding.
The Namoi River carves a 15 km gorge that drops 245 m; over 120 bird species have been recorded.
Billys Hole and Boundary Hole picnic areas are near Gum Hole campground, for bushwalking, birdwatching, fishing and canoeing on the Namoi, near Manilla north of Tamworth.
NPWS alerts: park fire ban until 31 Mar 2027; 1080 fox baiting 10 Aug-10 Dec 2026 (keep dogs restrained). No park entry fee (not on the fee-collecting list).

entries.name: Paul Wild Observatory

facts.claim: CSIRO: the Paul Wild Observatory Visitors Centre is self-guided, open 8.00am-5.00pm daily including public holidays, and entry is free.

Five of the Australia Telescope Compact Array's six 22 m dishes sit on a 3 km railway track in front of the visitors centre; the centre has indoor and outdoor exhibits and a small cinema; the observatory is about 25 km from Narrabri and 500 km from Sydney.
CSIRO asks visitors to switch phones and other devices to airplane mode and turn off Wi-Fi and Bluetooth; photography is welcome. Contact: Compact Array Visitors Centre +61 2 6790 4000.
Wikipedia: the observatory, about 24 km west of Narrabri, is the home of the Australia Telescope Compact Array (operating since 1988) and the Culgoora Solar Observatory.

entries.name: Pilliga Hot Artesian Bore Baths

facts.claim: Pilliga Artesian Bore Bath: 37 C mineral-rich water, "Open 24 hours a day"; the bore was built in 1902 as the town water supply and the pool installed in 1980; it is also a primitive campground ($7 per site per night, maximum stay four nights); Pilliga is 105 km west of Narrabri.

VisitNSW: just east of Pilliga village on the Pilliga Road; "There is no charge to enter the Bore for a day visit"; a toilet block, cold shower, electric barbecue and shelters; a roof covers the pool, which is lit for night bathing; water about 37.1 C.
The NSW Government visitor listing (403 to the fetch tool, read through search) lists a price of $5, likely the older camping rate; the tourism board gives $7.

Burning Mountain (Mount Wingen) takes its name from a smouldering coal seam running underground through the sandstone; a trail with information panels runs from the parking lots to where smoke emanates from the ground.
